text: Scene 6
speaker: N/A

text: Scene 6 - A room at the Bristol
speaker: C1

text: Basil Hallward was shown into a little private room at the Bristol where dinner had been laid for three.
speaker: C2

text: Lord Henry waited, eager to speak to his friend.
speaker: C1

text: I suppose you have heard the news?
speaker: Lord Henry

text: What is it? Nothing about politics, I hope! They don’t interest me. There is hardly a single person in the House of Commons worth painting, though many of them would be the better for a little whitewashing.
speaker: Basil

text: Dorian is engaged to be married,
speaker: Lord Henry

text: Engaged! Impossible! To whom?
speaker: Basil

text: To some little actress or other.
speaker: Lord Henry

text: I can't believe it. He is far too sensible.
speaker: Basil

text: He is far too wise not to do foolish things now and then, my dear Basil.
speaker: Lord Henry

text: Marriage is hardly a thing that one can do now and then, Harry.
speaker: Basil

text: Except in America. But I didn't say he was married. I said he was engaged to be married. There is a great difference.
speaker: Lord Henry

text: It would be absurd for him to marry so much beneath him.
speaker: Basil

text: If you want to make him marry this girl, tell him that.
speaker: Lord Henry

text: I hope the girl is good, Harry. I don't want to see Dorian tied to some vile creature, who might degrade his nature and ruin his intellect.
speaker: Basil

text: Oh, she is better than good, she is beautiful. Dorian says she is beautiful, and he is not often wrong about things of that kind.
speaker: Lord Henry

text: But do you approve of it? You can't approve of it. It is some silly infatuation.
speaker: Basil

text: I never approve, or disapprove, of anything now. It is an absurd attitude to take towards life. We are not sent into the world to air our moral prejudices. I hope that Dorian will make this girl his wife, passionately adore her for six months, and then suddenly become fascinated by someone else. He would be a wonderful study. But here is Dorian. He will tell you more than I can.
speaker: Lord Henry

text: My dear Harry, my dear Basil, you must both congratulate me. I have never been so happy. Of course, it is sudden and yet it seems to me to be the one thing I have been looking for all my life.
speaker: Dorian

text: I hope you will be happy Dorian but I don’t quite forgive you for not letting me know of your engagement. You let Harry know.
speaker: Basil

text: Come, you will tell us how it all came about.
speaker: Lord Henry

text: After I left you yesterday evening, Harry, I went down to the theatre. Sibyl was playing Rosalind. You should have seen her! When she came on in her boy's clothes, she was perfectly wonderful. She had never seemed to me more exquisite. As for her acting - well, you shall see her tonight. After the performance was over, I went behind and spoke to her. As we were sitting together, suddenly there came into her eyes a look that I had never seen there before. My lips moved towards hers. We kissed each other. Of course, our engagement is a secret. She has not even told her own mother. I don't know what my guardians will say. I don't care. I shall be of age in less than a year, and then I can do what I like.
speaker: Dorian

text: At what particular point did you mention marriage?
speaker: Lord Henry

text: I did not treat it as a business transaction, and I did not make any formal proposal. I told her that I loved her, and she said she was not worthy to be my wife. Not worthy! Why, the whole world is nothing to me compared with her.
speaker: Dorian

text: Women are wonderfully practical - much more practical than we are. In situations of that kind we often forget to say anything about marriage, and they always remind us.
speaker: Lord Henry

text: Don't, Harry. You have annoyed Dorian. He is not like other men. He would never bring misery on anyone
speaker: Basil

text: Dorian is never annoyed with me. I have a theory that it is always the women who propose to us, and not we who propose to the women.
speaker: Lord Henry

text: You are quite incorrigible, Harry; but I don't mind. It is impossible to be angry with you. When you see Sibyl Vane, you will feel that the man who could wrong her would be a beast, a beast without a heart. When I am with her, I regret all that you have taught me. I become different from what you have known me to be. and the mere touch of Sibyl’s hand makes me forget you and all your wrong fascinating, poisonous, delightful theories.
speaker: Dorian

text: And those are …?
speaker: Lord Henry

text: Oh, your theories about life, about love, about pleasure. All your theories, in fact.
speaker: Dorian

text: Pleasure is the only thing worth having a theory about. Pleasure is Nature’s test, her sign of approval. When we are happy, we are always good, but when we are good, we are not always happy.
speaker: Lord Henry

text: Ah! but what do you mean by good?
speaker: Basil

text: To be good is to be in harmony with one's self. Discord is to be forced to be in harmony with others.
speaker: Lord Henry

text: Harry, you are dreadful! Come, let us go down to the theatre. When Sibyl comes on the stage you will have a new ideal of life. She will represent something to you that you have never known.
speaker: Dorian

text: I have known everything but I am always ready for a new emotion. Your wonderful girl may thrill me. I love acting. It is so much more real than life. Let us go - Dorian you will come with me. Basil there is only room for two in the brougham - you must follow in a hansom.
speaker: Lord Henry

text: The painter was silent and preoccupied. There was a gloom over him.
speaker: C1

text: He could not bear this marriage.
speaker: C2

text: A strange sense of loss came over him.
speaker: C4

text: He felt that Dorian Gray would never again be to him all that he had been in the past.
speaker: C4

text: Life had come between them.
speaker: All
